shared-pool.8: Find the insertion position without changing any links, so duplicates or a full pool can fail safely.
shared-pool.14: Detach the first free slot before attaching it to a live list; each slot must have exactly one owner.
shared-pool.32: Return the removed slot to the free chain so either list can reuse its capacity.

master-update.8: Hold one row from each input: storage stays bounded even when the files grow.
master-update.10: Choose the smaller pending key so output remains ordered without sorting the whole file.
master-update.15: Apply every transaction for this key in input order; a delete followed by an insert recreates the record.
master-update.23: Write once after all same-key changes; intermediate versions must never reach the output.

tournament-tree.13: Reject an unknown or previously reached ID: it represents a broken link, shared child or cycle.
tournament-tree.15: Mark the node before descending so a link back to an ancestor is detected.
tournament-tree.19: Reject disconnected records as well as invalid links reachable from the root.
tournament-tree.24: Change only the payload; child links and traversal structure remain unchanged.

word-paths.11: Check coordinates before indexing; Python's negative indices would otherwise wrap around incorrectly.
word-paths.18: Reject invalid direction letters before following the path, including the reserved start marker.
word-paths.25: Swap only when the next score is strictly greater. Equal-score paths keep their original order.

register-import.7: Validate the header before entering the write transaction so incompatible columns cannot be imported.
register-import.9: Commit the batch on normal exit; an unexpected database exception rolls back every insert in this call.
register-import.14: Strip all fields before checking them; keep quoted commas inside a CSV field intact.
register-import.18: Check existing IDs so the first valid record wins, including records already in the database.
